name: Cucumber slices
lead: Cucumber slices on the eyes are a traditional home beauty practice for puffy or tired-looking eyes, valued as a cool, moist compress. Cucumber is about 95% water.[1]

The Wikipedia pages on cucumbers and on puffy eyes reviewed here make no cosmetic claim for cucumber, so the practice is documented by custom rather than by research. A general cold-compress reference says cold can narrow blood vessels and ease swelling briefly.[2][3]

paras: Chilled slices are placed over closed eyes for a period. Raw cucumber is mostly water with small amounts of carbohydrate and protein, and vitamin K as its notable micronutrient.[1]

Any apparent effect is generally attributed to the cold and moisture, as with other cold compresses, rather than to cucumber itself. Cold is described as constricting vessels and reducing fluid leakage, presented as a short-term fix.[3] Cold compression evidence is mixed in injury settings.[2]
No studies found on cucumber slices for puffy or dark eyes.

lore.intro: Cucumber slices are a long-standing spa image and appear as a classic cold-compress option.

claims.claim: Cucumber slices reduce eye puffiness and dark circles
claims.believers: Proponents describe a cooling, soothing effect that leaves the area looking less swollen.
claims.experts: Reference sources on cucumber and puffiness make no such claim; cold in general is described as a short-term aid for swelling.[1][3]

card.summary: Classic spa cold compress for puffy eyes; any effect is from cold, and it is untested.
card.note: No research on cucumber for the eyes specifically.

quick.overview:
Cucumber slices over the eyes are a traditional remedy for puffy, tired-looking eyes.

No studies have tested them; any short-term effect is usually attributed to the cold.
quick.mechanism: Chilled, watery slices act as a mild cold compress that may briefly narrow vessels.
quick.risks: No specific harms documented; hygiene and eye contact with produce are general considerations.
